At 12.30 p.m. 16-4-38, a telephone call was received at the "Standard" office by the Advertising Manager named Woo Yoong Fee (胡裕飛) from a male Chinese who gave his name as Wong Kai Ming (王開明). The following conversation followed :-

Wong - "I am the person who telephoned you about ten days ago with a warning to be careful and am now in possession of valuable information which I can only confide to Mr. Nien, your General Manager. Could you call him to the phone? (See Diary 12 page 1, re previous telephone call)
Woo - "Mr. Nien is at present absent from the office, but will return at 5 p.m. What is the nature of your information?"
Wong - "My relation is employed by the Japanese and has full knowledge of the whole affair but I can only discuss the matter with Mr. Nien who I will telephone at 5 p.m. Should the Japanese discover that my relation has supplied this important information to me they will undoubtedly dismiss him so that should this happen could you guarantee him a position in your newspaper office?"
Woo - "Perhaps we could arrange it provided you supply us with the information."
Wong - "I will telephone Mr. Nien at 5 p.m."

The conversation then ceased and at 3 p.m. 16-4-38 Mr. Nien came to the station and reported the incident.

Mr. Nien was instructed and remained in his office between 4.45 p.m. and 6 p.m. 16-4-38 with a view to conversing with the man "Wong" as long as possible. D.S.I. Chang and the undersigned remained in the Telephone Company, Pekien Road, between the said times listening to all telephone calls to the Standard in an effort to have the source of this particular call traced. 1938年4月16日中午12时30分，《字林西报》（Standard）办公室广告经理胡裕飛（Woo Yoong Fee）接到一名自称王開明（Wong Kai Ming）的华籍男子打来的电话。对话内容如下：-

王：“我就是十天前打电话警告你们要小心的人，现在我掌握有价值的情报，只能向你们的总经理聂先生（Mr. Nien）透露。能否请他来接电话？（参见日记第12册第1页，关于之前的电话）”
胡：“聂先生目前不在办公室，但将在下午5点回来。你的情报性质是什么？”
王：“我的亲戚受雇于日本人，对整个事件了如指掌，但我只能与聂先生讨论此事，我将在下午5点给他打电话。如果日本人发现我的亲戚向我提供了这一重要情报，他们无疑会解雇他，因此如果发生这种情况，你能保证在他的报社里给他一个职位吗？”
胡：“如果你向我们提供情报，也许我们可以安排。”
王：“我将在下午5点给聂先生打电话。”

随后通话结束，1938年4月16日下午3时，聂先生来到警局报告了这一事件。

聂先生奉命行事，在1938年4月16日下午4时45分至6时之间留在其办公室内，以便尽可能长时间地与“王”姓男子交谈。警佐张（Chang）及本人在上述时间内留在北平路电话公司，监听所有打往《字林西报》的电话，试图追踪该特定电话的来源。然而，王

Reference to diary 11, page 15, para 3:

A report on the examination of fruit submitted to the
Shanghai Municipal Laboratory for analysis was received at
this station on 10-4-38 and reads as follows:-

ANALYSIS

Five oranges showed definite evidence of having been
punctured. One orange was abnormal. The expressed juice
of this orange had a definite alkaline reaction. It was
tested immediately for cyanide and arsenic group with
negative results. An average sample of all the suspected
fruits was submitted to toxicological examination. No
poisonous substance was detected. All recognised poisons
were tested for specifically.

OBSERVATIONS.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / 14 APR. 1938）

The only fruits showing definite evidence of puncture
were the oranges. None of the "Sunkist" brand showed
evidence of puncture. The oranges had been sprayed with
an alkaline borate probably as a preservative.

If cyanide had been added to the oranges it would be
so rapidly decomposed as to be chemically undetectable.

The decomposition product is non-toxic.

(Sgd) A.E. Fletcher, F.I.C.
ANALYST.

本捕房于1938年4月10日收到一份关于提交给上海公共租界工部局实验室进行分析的水果检验报告，内容如下：-

分析

五个橙子显示出明显的被刺穿痕迹。其中一个橙子异常。该橙子的榨汁液呈明显的碱性反应。立即对其进行了氰化物和砷类测试，结果为阴性。将所有可疑水果的平均样本提交进行毒理学检查。未检测到有毒物质。对所有已知毒药进行了专项测试。

观察结果.

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特科 / 1938年4月14日）

唯一显示出明显被刺穿痕迹的水果是橙子。“新奇士”（Sunkist）品牌的橙子均未显示被刺穿的痕迹。这些橙子可能作为防腐剂喷洒了碱性硼酸盐。

如果橙子中被添加了氰化物，它会迅速分解，以致在化学上无法检测。

分解产物无毒。

(签名) A.E. Fletcher, F.I.C.

Named Tsung Zeu Kung(曾耕耕), age 25, native of
Szechuen, Military, N.F.A.s-
Whilst two accomplices named Zau Soong Dau(趙松桃)
and Nyeh Bei Ming(葉培明), both armed with pistols,
made good their escape.
Dr. Liu when wounded, was about to proceed in the
omnibus to the temporary offices of the University of
Shanghai at 209 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, he being the President
of the said University.
The arrested man, in a statement, explained that he
and his two accomplices received instructions at the Head
quarters of the Special Service Corps, Chuen Han(川沙),
Pootung, to shoot and wound Dr. Liu who had been considered
a patriot until he recently changed his attitude and
became a traitor, this being based on the belief that he
was assuming the post of Civil Governor of the New
Government of Kiangsu.

March 28, 1938. Morning Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

ALLEGED POISONED FRUITS SENT TO "STANDARD"

At about 3 p.m. yesterday Zee Ah-yue (徐阿裕), native of Ningpo, teaboy No.30 employed by the Chai Loh Hotel (爵祿飯店) on Yu Ya Ching Road, brought three decorated baskets containing oranges, apples and pumeloes to the office of the "Standard" at No.436 Foochow Road. A careful examination of the baskets was made by one of the employees of the paper and three letters, badly typewritten in English with many words mis-spelt, were found in the baskets and were addressed to the editor and the editorial office of the paper. The letters, which were signed with a foreign name, read: "As a humble token of esteem for the patriotism and audacity of your paper in its articles, I send herewith three baskets of fruit which I ask you kindly to accept. I hope you will continue with your endeavours."

The employee summoned the Chinese detective and C.P.C's 1822 and 3135 posted by the Police at the office for protection. They detained the teaboy and took him and the three baskets of fruit to Louza Station. There an examination was made and it was discovered that each fruit had been pierced with a needle. When squeezed, a fluid believed to be poison flowed out. The fruit will be submitted for analysis.

The teaboy was interrogated and he made the following statement :- "At 10.20 a.m. to-day (March 27) two Japanese, accompanied by a Chinese, came to the Chai Loh Hotel and booked Room No.120 on the fourth floor. On the register the Chinese gave his name as Zung Kyung-piau (陳金表), age 22. He was about 30 years of age, dressed in a grey suit of foreign clothing and speaking the local dialect. One of the two Japanese was about 30 years of age, wearing a dark coat and grey trousers and the other, aged about 20, was attired in a grey suit of foreign clothing. They left after remaining in the room for a few minutes. At about 1 p.m. they returned to the hotel bringing with them four decorated baskets. They consumed two bottles of beer and ordered me to send one of the baskets first to House No.81, Yung Loh Faung (永樂坊), Bubbling Well Road, and the remaining three to the office of the 'Standard' on Foochow Road, adding that these baskets were gifts from a foreigner. I intended to tell a coolie to send them, but all the coolies were engaged as the hotel was crowded, it being Sunday. Therefore I took the baskets to the office of the 'Standard,' where I was arrested."

Chinese detective sergeants Leung Ching-daung (郎錦堂), Wong Shuan-ching (王善卿) and Tsu Soong-ling (朱松林) were detailed to visit the Chai Loh Hotel where they learned that the two Japanese and the Chinese, after sending the teaboy to take the baskets to the addresses mentioned, had hired a motor car (licence No.17822), driven by Koo Ning-sui (顧銘水), from the Mei Hwa Garage (美華汽車行) on Ningpo Road and were driven to the entrance of the Jessfield Park where they alighted. 《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

涉嫌向《字林西报》寄送毒水果

昨日下午3时许，宁波籍茶房徐阿裕（Zee Ah-yue），受雇于亚尔培路爵祿飯店（Chai Loh Hotel）之第30号茶房，将三只装饰精美的篮子送至福州路436号《字林西报》馆办公室，篮内装有橙子、苹果和柚子。该报一名职员仔细检查了篮子，在篮中发现三封信件，信件用英文打字，拼写错误甚多，字迹拙劣，收件人为该报编辑及编辑部。信件署名为一外国人名，内容如下：“贵报文章所展现之爱国精神与大胆无畏，令人钦佩，谨以此三篮水果作为微薄敬意，恳请笑纳。望贵报继续努力。”

该职员召来华捕，并通知派驻该报馆负责保护的巡捕1822号和3135号。他们扣留了茶房，将其连同三篮水果带至老闸捕房。经检查，发现每只水果均被针扎过。挤压时，流出一种疑似毒液的液体。水果将送交化验。

经讯问，茶房供称：“今日（3月27日）上午10时20分，两名日本人由一名中国人陪同来到爵祿飯店，预订了四楼120号房间。登记时，该中国人自称陈金表（Zung Kyung-piau），22岁。其实际年龄约30岁，身穿灰色西装，讲本地话。两名日本人中，一人约30岁，身穿深色外套和灰色长裤；另一人约20岁，身穿灰色西装。他们在房内停留几分钟后离开。下午1时许，他们带着四只装饰精美的篮子返回酒店。他们喝了两瓶啤酒，并吩咐我先将其中一只篮子送至静安寺路永樂坊（Yung Loh Faung）81号，其余三只送至福州路《字林西报》馆，并称这些篮子是一位外国人送的礼物。我本打算叫苦力送去，但因正值周日，酒店客满，所有苦力均有事在身。因此我亲自将篮子送至《字林西报》馆，随即被捕。”

华捕探长郎錦堂（Leung Ching-daung）、王善卿（Wong Shuan-ching）和朱松林（Tsu Soong-ling）奉命前往爵祿飯店调查，获悉两名日本人和那名中国人在吩咐茶房将篮子送往上述地址后，从宁波路美華汽車行（Mei Hwa Garage）租用了一辆汽车（牌照号17822），司机为顾銘水（Koo Ning-sui），乘车至兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）入口处下车。另经查证，这些篮子系于3月26日下午3时，由一名身穿和服的日本人和一名身穿蓝布长衫的中国人，以31.30元的价格在南京路永安公司购买。

Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

ATTEMPT TO SET FIRE TO PRINTING OFFICE OF "TA MEI WAN PAO
MORNING EDITION"

Since the withdrawal of the Chinese forces,
Shanghai has been living in an atmosphere of terrorism.
Newspapers are being threatened frequently and bombs have
become the common "present" to newspapers. On the afternoon
of March 27, an attempt was made to set fire to the printing
office of this paper.
The printing plant is located in the former
premises of the "Lih Pao" (立报). Its front door faces
Kiukiang Road, while the back door is in a narrow alleyway,
where printing paper is usually stored. There is a garbage
box nearby, which holds waste paper. An old woman undertakes
the cleaning of this narrow alleyway end of the back door
of the printing office.
At 1.20 p.m. yesterday, as the woman was cleaning
out the alleyway, she found, at the back door of the printing
office of this paper, a canvass newspaper bag lying by the
side of a roll of paper. The bag contained an old thermos
flask, three Ever-ready batteries and a small clock with
the hands indicating 1.30 and all were connected with a
piece of brass wire. When the woman shook the flask,
she heard a rattling and thinking that it was a broken
flask, she threw it into the garbage box and was startled
to hear a loud explosion. A fire broke out with dense
smoke and an unpleasant smell. The workers in the
printing office heard the explosion.
The bomb was found only ten minutes before the
time set for its explosion. The quantity of sulphur was
small, but it was sufficient to have caused great damage
owing to the amount of papers lying about the place.
The accidental discovery of the flask by the
aged woman will greatly discourage the plotters.

《大美晚报》晨刊及其他本地报纸：-

企图纵火焚烧《大美晚报》晨刊印刷厂

自中国军队撤离以来，上海一直笼罩在恐怖气氛之中。报纸频受威胁，炸弹已成为送给报社的常见“礼物”。3月27日下午，有人企图纵火焚烧本报印刷厂。

印刷厂位于原《立报》社址。前门面向九江路，后门位于一条狭窄弄堂内，通常在此存放印刷用纸。附近有一个垃圾箱，用于存放废纸。一位老妇人负责打扫印刷厂后门这条弄堂的尽头。

昨日下午1时20分，当该妇人在清理弄堂时，在本报印刷厂后门处，发现一个帆布报袋躺在一卷纸旁边。袋内装有一个旧热水瓶、三节“永备”牌电池和一个小闹钟，指针指向1点30分，所有物品均由一段铜丝连接。当该妇人摇晃热水瓶时，听到里面有响声，以为是个破瓶子，便将其扔进垃圾箱，随即听到一声巨响，大吃一惊。随后起火，浓烟滚滚，气味难闻。印刷厂的工人听到了爆炸声。

炸弹被发现时，距离预定爆炸时间仅十分钟。硫磺量虽少，但由于现场堆放大量纸张，足以造成巨大破坏。

老妇人偶然发现热水瓶，将极大挫败策划者的阴谋。

(1) A male Chinese, age about 40, stout build, round

(2) Male Chinese, age about 30, medium build, long

(3) Description not available.

The 1st and 2nd described approached C.P.C. 1361, who
was detailed for duty outside the "Standard" and was
standing about two yards West of the front entrance to
the premises, when the 1st described drew a revolver from
his pocket, pointed it at the C.P.C., and ordered him not
to move, at the same time the 2nd described snatched the
C.P.C's pistol and extracted the magazine from it. The
3rd man then threw two hand grenades of the "Potato Masher"
type into the offices of the Newspaper and two rapid
explosions followed.

The three assailants then ran to the said waiting
motor car, firing two shots in the direction of C.P.C. 1361
as they did so, and proceeded at a very high speed East
along Foochow Road.

One of the grenades exploded on the outside concrete
joist of the front entrance whilst the other grenade
exploded in the office at the lower part of the counter
near to the entrance Swing door, resulting in C.P.C. 1361
being wounded in the back and a pedestrian named Wong
Zien King (王全根), who was about 20 yards East from the
pages.zh:

(1) 一名中国男性，年龄约40岁，体格粗壮，圆脸，身穿长衫，头戴灰色毡帽，讲上海话。

(2) 一名中国男性，年龄约30岁，中等身材，长瘦脸，身穿黑色长衫，头戴灰色毡帽。

(3) 无体貌描述。

上述第1和第2名男子接近负责在《字林西报》馆外执勤的巡捕1361号，当时该巡捕正站在 premises 正门以西约两码处。第1名男子从口袋中掏出一把左轮手枪，指着该巡捕，命令其不许动，与此同时，第2名男子夺下该巡捕的手枪并取出弹夹。随后，第3名男子向报社办公室投掷了两枚“土豆捣碎器”式手榴弹，随即发生两次快速爆炸。

三名袭击者随后跑向等候的汽车，逃跑过程中向巡捕1361号方向开了两枪，然后沿福州路向东高速驶离。

其中一枚手榴弹在正门外的混凝土过梁上爆炸，另一枚在办公室内靠近入口旋转门的柜台下部爆炸，导致巡捕1361号背部受伤，一名名叫王全根（Wong Zien King）的行人也在距现场以东约20码处额头受伤。

C.P.C. 1361 was conveyed to the Police Hospital and

Chinese Hospital:-

Medical certificates read:-

(1)C.P.C. 1361:- Suffering from Shrapnel wound of
back. Will be detained in hospital for about
10 days.

(2)Wong Zien Rung(王全根):- Suffering from bruises
of face----Not serious----Not detained:

No employee of the newspaper was injured.

S.I. McLeod found on Foochow Road the magazine and
six rounds of ammunition which had been removed from the
pistol of C.P.C. 1361.

At about 12.05 a.m. 23-5-38, P.C. 104 Allen, attached
to Central Station, whilst in charge of a Mobile Search
Party, when passing the corner of Foochow Road and Shantung
Road in response to the explosion heard by him was
informed by a male Chinese S Yue Man(施彥萬)Private
watchman, employed at the Great China Dispensary, 313
Foochow Road, that there was a pistol lying on the foot-
path outside the dispensary. The pistol is a "Demon"
automatic, No. 62555 and 7 rounds of .32 cal. ammunition;
same was examined by the Finger Print Bureau but no
finger prints were found.

医学证明内容如下：-

(1) 巡捕1361号：- 背部受弹片伤。需住院约10天。

报社员工无人受伤。

1938年5月23日凌晨12时05分左右（原文日期疑有误，应为3月），中央捕房所属警员104号艾伦（Allen）率领流动搜查队，在听到爆炸声后途经福州路与山东路拐角处时，一名在大中华大药房（Great China Dispensary，福州路313号）任职的私人看守、中国男子施彥萬（S Yue Man）告知他，大药房外的人行道上有一把手枪。该手枪为“恶魔”牌自动手枪，编号62555，配有7发.32口径子弹；指纹局对该枪进行了检验，但未发现指纹。

observed a dark coloured M/car, Lic. No. 2924, came from
the direction of the shop where the bomb had been thrown,
at a very fast speed. The car proceeded from West to
East on Foochow Road, turning North into Shantung Road.
The Licence Number of this M/car was found to be
"Vacant" through the French Concession Traffic Office.
From enquiries made amongst pedestrians it was also
learned that M/car, Lic. No. 4246 had been seen on Foochow
Road, but this was ascertained to be false.(For further
particulars re this incident please see F.I.R. 1041/38L.)

27.3.38 AND HAS BEEN FULLY RECORDED AND ATTACHED
HERETO.

of each of the letters/nearly exactly similar as follows:-

"Lane 160, 33, Tifung Road,
Shanghai, March 27, 1938."

"Dear Sir,

I greatly admire your ability in always raising
a propaganda against the violent conduct of the Japanese
militarism.

**〔此处转录不清〕**
pages.zh:
11/9.

水果篮被交付，随后他返回查利酒店（Ohah Lah Hotel，原文拼写错误，应为Cha Leh）的120号房间，取走剩余的三篮水果，
此时相关人员已离开该房间。

乘坐同一辆公共黄包车，30号侍者（Runaboy，原文疑似Roomboy笔误）
前往福州路436号《标准》中文日报（"Standard" Chinese Language Daily Newspaper）办公室，
他试图交付水果，但如前所述被逮捕。

在每只篮子的水果顶部，发现了一封打字信件，收件人为：
编辑部主任，福州路436号，本地，
《文汇报》（Fun Wei Newspaper，原文拼写错误，应为Wen Wei）编辑部，福州路436号，本地，
以及《文汇报》编辑部主任，福州路436号，本地，
每封信的内容几乎完全相同，如下所示：

“上海，提篮桥路（Tifung Road，原文可能指Ti Feng Rd.或其他，暂按音译）33号160弄，
1938年3月27日。”

“尊敬的先生：

我非常钦佩您始终致力于宣传反对日本军国主义暴行的能力。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

pages.en:
11/10.

accept these fruits and henceforth to increase our relations
with the two countries, China and Britain.

I hope that you will keep on the propagandism of
the Japanese Militarism as thoroughly as possible.
I remain, Dear Sir,
Yours obediently,
(Signed) J. Matheson."

Each of the letters having purportedly been sent
by the same person, the telephone book was perused and a
name of G. Matheson, No.150/33 Tifeng Road was found re-
corded therein, (Telephone No.22124), the address con-
cerned was communicated with and resulted in Mrs. C. Mathe-
son being located, from whom it was learned that Mr. G.
Matheson of that address was already dead and therefore
could not have been the author of the letters.

In view of the above, it was suspected that the
fruit contained in the baskets had in some way been tam-
pered with, therefore a visit was made by detectives accom-
panying the puller of public ricksha, licence number 4968,
to No.81, Sun Avenue, Bubbling Well Road, where it was
learned that a large basket of fruit had been delivered to
that address at about 2.30 p.m. 27-5-38, but the intended
recipient not being at home the basket was deposited inside
the premises but not interfered with in any manner whatso-
ever.

A further typewritten letter in a similar strain
pages.zh:
11/10.

请收下这些水果，并从此增进我们中英两国之间的关系。

我希望您能尽可能彻底地继续宣传反对日本军国主义。
此致，
敬礼，
（签名）J. Matheson。”

由于每封信都声称由同一人寄出，查阅电话簿后发现，
提丰路（Tifeng Road）150/33号有一个G. Matheson的名字记录在案，（电话号码22124），
与该地址联系后，找到了C. Matheson夫人，
从中获悉该地址的G. Matheson先生已经去世，因此不可能是这些信件的作者。

鉴于上述情况，怀疑篮子里的水果以某种方式被动了手脚，
因此，侦探陪同牌照号为4968的公共黄包车车夫，
前往静安寺路孙科路81号，
得知一大篮水果已于1938年5月27日（原文日期可能有误，前文为3月27日）下午2点30分左右送达该地址，
但由于预期收件人不在家，篮子被放置在屋内，未受任何干扰。

另一封打字信件，语气与上述已获得的三封信相似

pages.en:
11/11.

to that of the three letters already obtained as above was
found in this basket, addressed to:-
Mr. T. O. Lin (刘湛恩),
81, Ah Leong,
Bubbling Well Road,
Shanghai.
and signed as the remainder, Mr. G. Lithgow, No.150/33
Tifeng Road.

Eventually the wife of the intended recipient of
this basket of fruit was located and when questioned stated
that she knew of no person by that name contained in the
letter likely to send her husband fruit or presents of such
a nature, the husband who's particulars are as follows:-
Lieu Tsai Ung (刘湛恩), age 41 years, Hopeh,
Roadmaster of the Shanghai University, present
address at No.269Yuen King Yuen Road,
he having been employed in this capacity for a period ex-
ceeding 13 years, he further claims that he is not con-
nected with any political party, or having any political
aspirations, he has not taken part in any activities that
could be associated with any such parties, governments or
societies and that he had not been approached by persons
known to have such connections, but on the [illegible] had
explained at some length, the explanation so presented did
not seem very convincing, but owing to an inter-
viewed with the delivery of this basket of fruit [illegible]

their surfaces as if made by a needle or some such similar
thin instrument, therefore it was considered probable that
some noxious substance had been injected into some of the
fruit.

The above resulted in the Finger Print Bureau being
informed and the immediate attendance of D.S. Kant and
D.P.S. Day who accompanied by D.S. Gigason proceeded to
Room No.120 of the Chak Lok Hotel, where a thorough exa-
mination of the room was conducted in an endeavour to ob-
tain latent prints of the late occupants of the room or
anything pertaining to their identity or activities.

Three small glasses inside the room which contained
various quantities of an amber coloured fluid, believed
to be beer, and two empty quart beer bottles were thus
examined and subsequently removed to this Station.

During the time of these latter enquiries it was
learned that some person, apparently a male Chinese had
communicated with the hotel by telephone to ascertain if the
delivery of the baskets containing the fruit had been ef-
fected, a reply asserting the affirmative being given
the communication terminated.

In view of the above and the lapse in the time of
vacating the room and the time of these enquiries it was
deemed useless to have detectives proceed to Joelifield

它们的表面，仿佛是由针或类似的细薄仪器造成的，
因此认为很可能有一些有害物质被注入到某些水果中。

上述情况导致指纹局接到通知，
警佐坎特（D.S. Kant）和副巡官戴（D.P.S. Day）立即到场，
并在警佐吉加森（D.S. Gigason）的陪同下前往查洛克酒店（Chak Lok Hotel，原文拼写不一致）的120号房间，
对该房间进行了彻底检查，试图获取房间前住客的潜在指纹
或与他们的身份或活动有关的任何物品。

检查了房间内的三个小玻璃杯，里面装有不同数量的琥珀色液体，
据信是啤酒，以及两个空的夸脱啤酒瓶，
随后将这些物品移至本警局。

在进行后一项调查期间，
得知有人（显然是一名中国男子）曾通过电话与酒店联系，
以确认装有水果的篮子是否已交付，
在得到肯定的答复后，通话结束。

鉴于上述情况，以及退房时间与调查时间之间的时间间隔，
认为让侦探前往极司菲尔路（Joelifield，原文拼写错误，应为Jessfield）已无用处

Park in order to try and locate the late passengers of his
motor car, license No.17822, therefore detectives were
posted for duty inside the room concerned with instructions
to inform this Station immediately should the persons con-
cerned return to the room or any other persons visit the
room, nothing resulting from this precaution the detectives
on this duty were withdrawn at about 12.30 a.m. 26-3-38.

The employees of the Wing On Company who had been
concerned in the purchase of the baskets of fruit attended
this Station prior to the contents of the baskets being
thoroughly examined and when they viewed same, were empha-
tic and sure in their assertions that these were the basket-
ets purchased by the two believed male Japanese and male
Chinese during the afternoon of the 26-3-38, but same had
been disturbed and re-arranged since the removal of the
baskets from the place of purchase.

During the morning of the 28-3-38, the whole of the
fruit together with the contents of the three glasses ob-
tained from room No.136 of the Chek Lok Hotel, was removed
to the S.M.C. Public Health Department, Hankow Road, for
purposes of being examined and submitted to tests to as-
certain the belief that some noxious substance had been
injected into some of the fruit or otherwise. A report
of this examination is expected to be received during the
course of the next three or four days.
pages.zh:

为了试图找到其汽车（牌照号17822）的前乘客，公园方面因此在相关房间内部署了侦探执行任务，并指示一旦相关人员返回该房间或有任何其他人造访该房间，须立即通知本警署。采取这一预防措施后未获任何结果，遂于1938年3月26日凌晨约12时30分撤回了执行此任务的侦探。

永安公司参与购买这几篮水果的雇员，在篮内物品被彻底检查之前来到本警署；当他们查看这些物品时，坚决且肯定地声称，这些就是1938年3月26日下午由两名据信为日本男子和中国男子所购买的篮子，但自从篮子从购买地移走后，里面的东西已被搅动并重新摆放过。

1938年3月28日上午，所有水果以及从捷乐旅馆（Chek Lok Hotel）136号房间取得的三个玻璃杯内的物品，均被送往汉口路的工部局公共卫生处，以便进行检查和测试，以证实有人向部分水果注射了有毒物质或其他类似情况的推测。预计在未来三至四天内收到此次检查的报告。

At 11.55 p.m. on the 22-3-38, a telephone
message was received from the Standard Chinese
Language Daily Newspaper Office, 435 Foochow Road,
reporting that a bomb had been thrown into the
premises.

The Station alarm was rung and all available
men from the Station attended with C.I. Shellswell
and C.D.I. Sharman.

D.J.C. "A" Division attended and the Reserve
Unit was called out.

The S.P.B. Ambulance was summoned and conveyed
C.P.C.1361 to the Police Hospital and a pedestrian
named Wong Lien Kung (王全根) to the Lester Chinese
Hospital.

Doctor's chits read as follows:-

"C.P.C.1361 - Suffering from shrapnel wound of
back. Will be detained in hospital about 10
days".

"Wong Zien Kung - Suffering from Bruices of face.
Not serious." Not detained.

Enquiries were made by C.D.S.85, C.D.C.s 37, 82,
127 and the undersigned, and the following was ascer-
tained.

C.P.C.1361 was detailed for duty outside the
Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper, No.436
Foochow Road, and he was standing about two yards to
the West of the front entrance to the premises. At
about 11.50 p.m. even date, a closed motor car,
license number unknown, stopped about four yards to
the East of the front entrance and about 1½ yards
from the footpath. Three male Chinese description
as on Sheet No.1 of this report, left the motor car.

Two of them (the 1st and 2nd described) came near the C.P.C., when the 1st described drew a revolver (believed to be a .45 calibre "Webley" revolver) from his pocket, pointed at the C.P.C. and ordered him not to move, at the same time the 2nd described grabbed the C.P.C's pistol and extracted the magazine from same. The 3rd man then threw two grenades of the "Potato Masher" type into the offices of the newspaper and two rapid explosions followed.

The three assailants then ran to the motor car firing two shots in the direction of C.P.C.1361 and proceeded in a very high speed East along Foochow Road.

One of the grenades exploded on the outside concret joist of the front entrance whilst the other grenade exploded in the office on the lower part of the counter just in front of the swing door, resulting in wounding C.P.C.1361 in the back and the above named pedestrian, who was about 20 yards East from the scene of the explosion, in the forehead, damaging all glass of the show windows and the glass of the swing door by the fragments of the grenade and concussion. Slight damage done to the walls of the offices and the counter. Some fragments of the bomb had penetrated the ceiling and were found in the two small offices on the 1st floor.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Inspector McLeod found on Foochow Road the magazine and six rounds of ammunition from the pistol of C.P.C.1361, which was taken away by the 2nd described assailants

No person was in the ground floor offices during the explosion, therefore no employee of the newspaper received any injuries.

The proprietor, publisher and editor of the newspaper, is Mr. H.M. Curine (British) whilst the general manager is Mr. P.L. Hien. None of them was in the offices at the time of the explosion, but the latter named arrived later being informed of the occurrence by the employees. About 10 employees were in the upper floor of the premises and heard two explosions. The vicinity of the scene of the explosion was searched by the Reserve Unit under charge of Assistant Commissioner, Mr. Fairbairn but proved abortive in the arrest of any person connected with this crime.

A similar offence occurred at the same premises on the 10-2-38 (Please see F.I.R.536/38)Louza).

About one week ago Woo received a telephone call

《标准报》总经理，自该报社开业以来才从事报纸工作，因此，鉴于胡经验丰富，上海报界人士普遍视胡为《标准报》的“机制”，此为比喻说法。

今日在捕房受讯时，胡透露了上述事实，但在提供信息方面显得非常缄默，并声称从未受到任何个人或组织的接触或威胁。然而，他最终承认如下情况：-

在他（胡）拥有《社会日报》期间，中央政府曾向各家报社发放津贴，他通过一位名叫錢考慶（Zien Kya Zung）的人每月为《社会日报》领取100.00美元，此人与一家名为《新顺报》（Shin Shun Pao）的报纸有关，该报由日本人拥有。

大约一周前，胡接到上述錢考慶的电话，要求他在南京路的孙雅餐厅（Sun Yah Restaurant）与其会面。次日约定时间，胡在该餐厅与钱见面，钱解释说他正在协助在南京建立临时政府。随后，他要求他（胡）在《标准报》刊登

pages.en:
10/Sheet No. 3.

news or telegrams concerning the said Government in the
"Standard" newspaper. Zien added that should he agree to
comply with this request the Japanese would grant $400.00
per month to the "Standard" newspaper. In answer Woo replied
that as he was only the Advertising Manager of the concern
he could not give an opinion but that he would convey the
information to Mr. Cumine, Proprietor, and Mr. Nien, General
Manager. Woo and Zien then separated and, on the same date,
Woo informed Mr. Cumine and Mr. Nien who rejected the offer.
Questioned as to whether he thought the series of
recent incidents which occurred at the "Standard" had any
bearing on Zien's proposal Woo stated that he did and that
it was possible that should the offer have been accepted
the "Standard" would no longer be a target of terrorist
activities.
At this point of the information Woo definitely
refused to reveal further details and, regretting having
spoken in regard to the matter, he pleaded that the
information be kept secret and not made the subject of
a report. Questioned as to his fear Woo stated that should
it become known to certain elements that he had given the
said information to police it would probably mean his death
and also the death of Zien Eye Sung.
Mr. Nien, who was present in the station, stated
pages.zh:
10/第3页。

有关该政府的新闻或电报时，停止在“南京临时政府”标题上使用“括号”。钱补充说，如果他同意遵守这一要求，日本人将每月给予《标准报》400.00美元。胡回答说，由于他只是该机构的广告经理，他无法发表意见，但会将此信息转达给业主库明（Cumine）先生和总经理聂（Nien）先生。胡与钱随后分开，同日，胡告知库明先生和聂先生，他们拒绝了这一提议。
当被问及他认为最近发生在《标准报》的一系列事件是否与钱的提议有关时，胡表示有关，并指出如果接受该提议，《标准报》可能不再成为恐怖活动的目标。
在此阶段，胡坚决拒绝透露更多细节，并对谈及此事表示后悔，他恳求将此信息保密，不作为报告的主题。当被问及他的恐惧时，胡表示，如果某些势力得知他向警方提供了上述信息，这可能意味着他和钱义松（Zien Eye Sung，音译）的死亡。
当时在捕房的聂先生陈述

pages.en:
10/Sheet No. 4.

that the information given by Woo was correct but he also
could not give further details for reasons as stated by Woo.
Mr. Cumine, also corroborated Woo's statement but,
when further questioned, he stated that he had to leave
the station immediately, and departed.
The Shing Ya Society mentioned in the Translation,
it is assumed, refers to the Pro-Asiatic Movement which
originated in Japan several years ago.
Mr. Woo refused to write a statement in regard to
the incident and it is noted that Zien acted by telephone,
and then verbally in the absence of witnesses.
Woo is evidently reticent in giving information
on account of being afraid but further persuasion might
lead to him revealing the whereabouts of Zien.
In the meantime C.P.C.s on duty in the vicinity of
Woo's home are being instructed to keep the house under
observation.
Enquiries proceeding.

胡提供的信息是正确的，但由于胡所述的原因，他也无法提供更多细节。
库明先生也证实了胡的陈述，但在进一步询问时，他表示必须立即离开捕房，随即离去。
译文中提到的兴亚会（Shing Ya Society），据推测是指几年前起源于日本的兴亚运动（Pro-Asiatic Movement）。
胡先生拒绝就此事书写供词，值得注意的是，钱是通过电话行事，然后在没有证人的情况下口头交谈。
胡显然因害怕而在提供信息方面保持缄默，但进一步劝说可能会促使他透露钱的下落。
与此同时，正在指示在胡家附近执勤的中央巡捕对该房屋进行监视。
调查正在进行中。

J.D.S. Kobayashi, D.S.I. Chang and the undersigned
interviewed Mr. Chow Vung Sui(          ), Compradore of
the Taiwan Bank and Committee Member of The Shanghai
Citizens Association, on the morning of 3-3-38. He was
located in the said Association offices in the Yokohama
Specie Bank Building, The Bund.

Questioned as to the significance of the words
"Chow( 周 ), Representative of the Slave Bank" on the card
Mr. Chow Vung Sui stated that he could think of no reason
why the card should bear any reference to him, except
for the fact that he is a Japanese subject and has been
connected with the Taiwan Bank for about thirty years.

On being further questioned, however, Mr. Chow
stated that at the commencement of the local hostilities
he received a threatening letter, per post, at the Taiwan
Bank, warning him to cease being connected with the said
bank under threats of death. He could not recall the
contents of the letter but was of the opinion that it had
been signed by some "Traitor Extermination Group". On
receipt of the letter he destroyed it and made no report
to police in regard to it, but since that time he has kept
away from the Bank as much as possible and has confined
most of his time to the Shanghai Citizens Association office

No further incident occurred until on or about
pages.zh:
8/第2页。

小林（Kobayashi，音译）警司、张（Chang）高级督察及本人于1938年3月3日上午会见了台湾银行买办、上海市民协会委员周云水（Chow Vung Sui，音译）先生。会面地点位于外滩横滨正金银行大楼内的该协会办公室。

当被问及卡片上“周（Chow），奴隶银行代表”字样的含义时，周云水先生表示，他想不出卡片提及他的任何理由，除非是因为他是日本臣民，且与台湾银行有约三十年的关联。

然而，在被进一步询问时，周先生表示，在当地战事开始时，他在台湾银行收到一封通过邮局寄来的恐吓信，警告他停止与该银行的关联，否则将面临死亡威胁。他记不清信件的具体内容，但认为落款是某个“锄奸团”。收到信后，他将信销毁，未向警方报告，但自那以后，他尽可能远离银行，大部分时间都待在上海市市民协会办公室。

此后未发生其他事件，直到大约

pages.en:
8/Sheet No. 3.

the 14-2-38 when Mr. Chow received a further threatening
letter, the post office mark being dated 14-2-38. The
letter was addressed to Mr. Chow, c/o The Bank of Taiwan,
and was signed "Wong Dah Chong". No person of this name
is known to Mr. Chow.

In the letter the writer accused Mr. Chow of being
a Chinese Traitor and warned him against the following
points:-

(1) "Do not support the Japanese or co-operate
with them any longer."

(2) "Do not give the Japanese any facility to form
any kind of organization. Endeavour to destroy
Japanese activities."

The letter terminates by warning Mr. Chow that
someone is attempting to take a final measure against
him.

Subsequent to the said detectives' interview with
Mr. Chow he located the latter letter referred to, and
handed it to D.S. Kobayashi who is dealing with the case
and has forwarded the letter to Headquarters for examina-
tion and comparison.

1938年2月14日左右，周先生收到了另一封恐吓信，邮戳日期为1938年2月14日。信件寄给周先生，由台湾银行转交，落款为“Wong Dah Chong（音译）”。周先生不认识叫这个名字的人。

信中作者指控周先生是中国汉奸，并警告他注意以下几点：

(1) “不要再支持日本人或与他们合作。”

(2) “不要为日本人组建任何类型的组织提供便利。努力破坏日本人的活动。”

信件最后警告周先生，有人正试图对他采取最终措施。

在上述侦探会见周先生之后，他找到了这封后来提到的信，并将其交给负责此案的警司小林（Kobayashi），后者已将信送往总部进行检验和比对。

1938年2月26日下午3点左右，一名身穿西式服装、只会说英语的中国男子来到他家，编造故事称他刚从美国抵达，说手头缺钱，请求给他一些钱，直到他从美国收到预付款。

当时 Cumine 先生不在家，但该陌生人被他的客人 Ward 先生看到，Ward 先生是一位年迈的病患。

floor.
The door was opened by Mr. Cumine's servant Ah Nyi
( 阿 二 ). The stranger asked the servant if his master
was in. The servant thereupon asked him first in Chinese
and, as he did not appear to understand, then in English,
for his card. The stranger had no card but wrote down
the name "Francis K. Woo" in English on a piece of paper.
This piece of paper was shown to Mr. Ward, and the visitor
ushered in. He stayed and talked to Mr. Ward for about
20 minutes, and gave the following story:-
Ten days ago he had arrived from San Francisco,
where his father has a curio store. He had come to
Shanghai to do business for his father, but had run short
of money. He was staying at a Chinese Hotel, and wanted
cash to pay his hotel bill for the past several days.
Mr. Ward informed him he was not the house-holder.
The visitor then asked for the house owner or the "press-
man" (Mr. Cumine is the owner of a Chinese newspaper
"The Standard" ( 文 匯 報 )). He was informed
he was not in.
At about this time, another visitor called to see
Mr. Ward, and the stranger left.
It was noticed that on his way out he gave a long
look at the premises, as though he meant to identify some
future move.

公寓。
门由 Cumine 先生的仆人阿二（Ah Nyi）打开。陌生人问仆人主人是否在家。仆人随即先用中文问他，见他似乎听不懂，又用英文向他要名片。陌生人没有名片，但在一张纸上用英文写下了“Francis K. Woo”的名字。这张纸给 Ward 先生看过，随后访客被引入。他停留并与 Ward 先生交谈了约20分钟，讲述了以下故事：
十天前他从旧金山抵达，他父亲在那里有一家古玩店。他来上海是为父亲做生意，但钱用完了。他住在一家中国旅馆，需要现金支付过去几天的旅馆账单。
Ward 先生告诉他，自己不是户主。
访客随后要求见房东或“报馆老板”（Cumine 先生是一家中文报纸《文汇报》的所有者）。他被告知主人不在。
大约在此时，另一位访客来拜访 Ward 先生，陌生人便离开了。
注意到他在离开时长时间打量了房屋，似乎意在识别某些未来的行动目标。

Mr. Cumine is worried over this incident because
recently he has received several anonymous letters at his
downtown office, and has been the target of certain
terrorist activities.
A uniform constable has been placed on duty at his
home pending a private watchman there being armed.
Enquiries proceeding.

My name is Hsu Kung Zeu, age 38 years, native of Wusieh,

At about 1.30 p.m. to-day (1-3-38) I observed that the shop
assistant Yang Sau Ling was attending to two male Chinese customers,

clothing, who wanted to purchase two boxes of American oranges.
Subsequently the one in Chinese clothing came near to the counter
and paid to me two $5.00 notes, and asked me to give him two pieces
of plain paper and a Chinese pen. I did so and the man wrote some-
thing but as I was busy at that time I did not notice what he wrote
on the paper. Afterwards the man gave the paper to Yang Su Ling.
At 3.30 p.m. I ordered the shop apprentice Wong Chuh Sung to deliver
the goods.

The above is my true statement.
(Signed) Hsu Kung Zeu.

The following is the statement of Yang Sau Ling,
native of Shanghai, taken by me C.D.S.134,
at Louza Station on the 1-3-38, and translated and interpreted by Clerk Wu Pang Yao.

My name is Yang Sau Ling, age 38 years, native of Shang-hai, S/shop assistant, employed at the Sing Pau Foong Fruit Shop situated at No.433, Honan Road. I have been employed in this shop for about one year.

At about 1.30 p.m. to-day (1-3-38) two male Chinese, one dressed in foreign style clothing, and the other in Chinese clothing, came to the shop. The one in Chinese clothing informed me that he wanted to purchase two boxes of American oranges. I told him that the price was $5.00 per box. This man then produced two $5.00 notes from his pocket and handed same to the accountant of the shop named Hsu Kung Zeu. He then asked the accountant to give him two pieces of plain paper and a Chinese pen and on the paper he wrote the following two addresses:-
(1) To the Manager Office, No.19, Avenue Edward VII, French Concession. - Sent by Staff., and
(2) To Mr. Cusine, No.436, Foochow Road - Sent by Staff.

After this the man gave me two flask containers which were wrapped with papers printed with the name of the "Wing On Coy.,Ltd., and requested that same should be sent along with the oranges to the above two addresses at 4.00 p.m. today without fail. The accountant Hsu Kung Zeu then, at about 3.30 p.m. even date, ordered the apprentice Wong Chuh Sung to send the said goods by the shop's bicycle to the given addresses, and this accordingly did. The above is my true statement.

(Signed) Yang Sau Ling.

Description of the two males concerned as follows:-
1. Age about 35, height 5'6", medium build, square sallow face, wearing a grey serge long gown and a grey felt hat, speaking Shanghai dialect.
2. Age about 23/24, height 5'5", medium build, square sallow face, wearing navy blue foreign style suits, white shirt, grey necktie, long hair brushed backwards.

今天下午（1938年3月1日）约1点30分，两名中国男子来到店里，一人穿西式服装，另一人穿中式服装。穿中式服装的人告诉我他想购买两箱美国橙子。我告诉他价格是每箱5.00元。那人随后从口袋里掏出两张5.00元钞票，交给店里名为许根寿的会计。然后他让会计给他两张白纸和一支毛笔，他在纸上写了以下两个地址：-

之后，那人交给我两个用印有“永安有限公司”名称的纸包裹的热水瓶容器，并要求务必在今天下午4点将上述物品随橙子一起送至上述两个地址。同日约下午3点30分，会计许根寿命令学徒黄竹松用店里的自行车将所述货物送往指定地址，黄随即照办。以上是我的真实陈述。

The following is the statement of Wong Chuh Sung,

at Louza Station on the 1-3-38, translated and interpreted by Clerk Liu Pang Yao.

My name is Wong Chun Sung, age 19 years, native of Soochow, S/apprentice employed at the Sing Pau Foong Fruit Shop, No.433, Honan Road.

At about 3.00 p.m. to-day (1-3-38) the accountant of the shop named Hsu Ming Tzu handed me four articles of goods (2 boxes of oranges and 2 boxes allegedly containing flasks) together with two papers bearing addresses and ordered me to send one box of each to the given address by the the shop's bicycle. The addresses on the paper were:-
(1) Mr. Cumine, No.436 Foochow Road. and
(2) The Manager, No.19, Avenue Edward VII, Frenchtown.

I left the shop at about 3.25 p.m. and first proceeded to the Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper Office, No. 436, Foochow Road. On arriving there I left the bicycle outside the premises and sent in one of each boxes into the Standard Newspaper Office. The staffs of the Standard Newspaper refused to accept the goods and called a policeman who brought me to the Station.

The above is my true statement.

(Signed) Wong Chuh Sung.

本人姓名 Wong Chun Sung，年龄 19 岁，苏州籍，受雇于河南路 433 号新宝丰水果店（Sing Pau Foong Fruit Shop）之学徒。

今日（1938 年 3 月 1 日）下午约 3 时，本店会计徐明子（Hsu Ming Tzu）交给我四件货物（2 箱橙子及 2 箱据称装有烧瓶的物品），连同两张写有地址的纸条，命令我使用店内的自行车将每种箱子各一个送至指定地址。纸条上的地址为：
(1) 福州路 436 号 Cumine 先生收。及
(2) 法租界爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）19 号经理收。

我于下午约 3 时 25 分离开店铺，首先前往福州路 436 号《标准日报》（Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper）馆。到达后，我将自行车留在门外，并将每样箱子各一个送入《标准日报》馆。《标准日报》馆职员拒绝接收货物，并叫来一名警察将我带至捕房。

以上属实。

（签名）Wong Chuh Sung。

The post card was passed by complaint to the
Special Branch who forwarded it to this Station on 24-2-38

and the undersigned made enquiries at the said newspaper
office but the staff, including Mr. P. L. Hien, General
Manager, were unable to give any solution as to the pur-

来自“正义团”（Righteousness Corps），象征着已无话可说，并将采取行动。
    然而，“周（Chow），奴隶银行代表”这几个字具有特殊意义，对此我提出以下推测。
    日本商号台湾银行（Taiwan Bank），地址位于外滩 16 号，其买办名为周云水（Chow Vung Sui，原文不清），他同时也是上海市民协会（The Shanghai Citizens Association）的委员，该协会是一个日本组织，办公地点位于外滩横滨正金银行大楼。明信片作者知晓周与上述利益集团的关系，因此可能寄出此明信片给《标准日报》，预设他们会在报纸刊物中提及该卡片，特别是“奴隶银行代表周”这一名字，从而间接警告周，表明作者已知晓其身份。
    该明信片正送交总局进行检查。
    需采取后续行动。

At 6.18 p.m. 10-2-38 a telephone message was
received from C.C.R. to the effect that a bomb had
been thrown into No. 436, Foochow Road, and that an
inmate had been injured.

The station alarm was sounded and all avail-
able police attended with C.I. Shellswell. The
S.F.B. ambulance was summoned; The Reserve Unit was
notified; The D.O."A" and D.D.O."A" were informed.

Enquiries by C.D.S. 47, C.D.C.s 237, 23 and
the undersigned revealed as follows:-

The scene of offence is the office of The
Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper, No. 436,
Foochow Road, located about 30 yards East of Fukien
Road. The ground floor is the Circulating and
Advertising department and is approximately 24 ft.
x 19 ft. in dimension, fitted with a double swing
door which faces Foochow Road.

A counter, approximately 3 ft. high, extends
along the office in close proximity to the front
door, and then along the East side of the office,
there being sufficient space between this counter
and the walls for customers. The office is equipped
with four flat topped desks. The rear and side
walls are entirely covered by glass cases.

The proprietor, publisher and editor of
the newspaper is Mr. H.M. Cumine, (British) whilst
the General Manager is a male named P.L. Nien. A
staff of one cashier, three accountants, six
assistants and one manager are employed. The
pages.zh:
1938 年 2 月 10 日下午 6:18，接到中央无线电室（C.C.R.）的电话消息，称有人向福州路 436 号投掷炸弹，且有一名内部人员受伤。

站内警报响起，所有可用警力在刑事侦缉督察 Shellswell 带领下到场。召来了工部局消防队（S.F.B.）救护车；通知了后备队；通报了“A”区分区督察（D.O."A"）及副分区督察（D.D.O."A"）。

经警员 C.D.S. 47、刑事侦缉警长 C.D.C.s 237、23 及本人查询，结果如下：-

案发地点为福州路 436 号《标准中文日报》馆办公室，位于福建路以东约 30 码处。底层为发行部和广告部，尺寸约为 24 英尺 x 19 英尺，配有面向福州路的双扇弹簧门。

一个高约 3 英尺的柜台沿办公室靠近前门处延伸，然后沿办公室东侧延伸，柜台与墙壁之间留有足够空间供顾客使用。办公室内设有四张平顶办公桌。后墙和侧墙完全覆盖着玻璃展示柜。

该报的所有人、出版人及编辑为 H.M. Cumine 先生（英国人），总经理为一名名叫 P.L. Nien 的男子。雇佣了一名出纳、三名会计、六名助理和一名经理。该

pages.en:
1/sheet No. 3.

papers are printed by the Ta Kung Pao Press, 181, Avenue
Edward VII, French Concession.

At about 6.00p.m. 10-2-38 seven employees were work-
ing in the office when a male Chinese, described on Sheet
No. 1, suddenly pushed the front swing door open and
advanced towards the counter, then threw a hand grenade of the
potato masher type. The missile glided along the top of a
desk which extended from the counter, then struck an
apprentice named Fang Tse Ching (方志勤), age 22, native
of Shanghai, in the abdomen, and fell to the cement floor.
This apprentice then ran for about ten feet through the
rear door of the office when he heard an explosion, it
later being discovered that the following three inmates
had been injured:-

(1) Sung Deng Hsien (宋桐軒), age 54, native of
Kashing, m/clerk.
(2) Siau Yue Ching (蕭由卿), age 37, native of
Soochow, m/assistant in the advertising depart-
ment.
(3) Pih Ts Fong (畢礼芳), age 23, native of Ningpo,
m/apprentice.

Damage on a fairly large scale was caused to the
desks and wall show cases whilst the front windows were
smashed, the damage having been caused by the bomb fragments
and concussion.

The three injured employees were removed in the
S.P.B. ambulance to The Lester Chinese Hospital where they
pages.zh:
1/第 3 页。

报纸由法租界爱多亚路 181 号《大公报》印刷厂（Ta Kung Pao Press）印刷。

1938 年 2 月 10 日下午约 6:00，七名员工正在办公室工作时，一名如第 1 页所述的华裔男子突然推开前部弹簧门，走向柜台，随后投掷了一枚马铃薯捣碎器型手榴弹。该投射物沿着一张从柜台延伸出的办公桌顶部滑行，然后击中了一名名叫方志勤（Fang Tse Ching）的学徒的腹部，方志勤，22 岁，上海籍，随后掉落在混凝土地板上。这名学徒听到爆炸声后，穿过办公室后门跑了约十英尺，后来发现以下三名内部人员受伤：-

(1) 宋桐轩（Sung Deng Hsien），54 岁，嘉兴籍，男职员。
(2) 萧由卿（Siau Yue Ching），37 岁，苏州籍，男广告部助理。
(3) 毕礼芳（Pih Ts Fong），23 岁，宁波籍，男学徒。

办公桌和墙面展示柜遭受了较大规模的损坏，前窗玻璃破碎，这些损坏是由炸弹碎片和冲击波造成的。

三名受伤员工由工部局警务处（S.P.B.）救护车送往莱斯特华人医院，在那里他们

pages.en:
1/Sheet No. 4.

were certified to be suffering from:-

(1) Sung Dong Hsien:- "Compound fracture of left
foot - very serious. Will require about 40
days treatment in Hospital".

(2) Siau Yue Ching:- "Compound fracture of right
hand and bomb wound of thigh - will require
about 20 days treatment in Hospital".

(3) Pih Ts Feng:- "Bomb wound back, chest and legs,
- may become serious - will require about
10 days treatment.(Not detained)."

Small fragments of the grenade penetrated the
ceiling and were found in two upstairs small offices
occupied by Mr. Cumine and the General Manager, Mr. P.L.
Hien. The latter was in his upstairs office when the
incident occurred but Mr. Cumine had left about one hour
previously.

Of all the inmates the only one who had noticed
the culprit enter , throw the grenade, and decamp, was
the apprentice Fang Tse Ching from whom a statement
has been taken and is attached. He states that he would
be able to identify the man, if arrested.

Discreet enquiries were conducted in the vicinity
but no person was located who could supply any further
information or assistance.

Mr. Cumine, when questioned, stated that during the
afternoon of 9-8-56 an anonymous letter, bearing the
Carter Road post office mark, had been delivered at the
office and that he had, on the same date, handed it to
pages.zh:
1/第 4 页。

被确诊患有：-

(1) 宋桐轩（Sung Dong Hsien）：- “左脚复合性骨折 - 非常严重。需要在医院治疗约 40 天”。

(2) 萧由卿（Siau Yue Ching）：- “右手复合性骨折及大腿炸弹伤 - 需要在医院治疗约 20 天”。

(3) 毕礼芳（Pih Ts Feng）：- “背部、胸部及腿部炸弹伤，- 可能恶化 - 需要治疗约 10 天。（未留院）。”

手榴弹的小碎片穿透天花板，在 Cumine 先生和总经理 P.L. Hien 先生占用的两间楼上小办公室内被发现。事发时后者在其楼上办公室内，但 Cumine 先生已在约一小时前离开。

在所有内部人员中，唯一注意到罪犯进入、投掷手榴弹并逃离的是学徒方志勤，已录取其供词并附后。他表示，如果该男子被捕，他能够指认。

在周边进行了谨慎的查询，但未找到能提供任何进一步信息或协助的人员。

Cumine 先生在接受询问时表示，1938 年 2 月 9 日下午，一封盖有卡德路邮局邮戳的匿名信被送至办公室，他在同日将其交给了

pages.en:
1/Sheet No. 5.

the S.M.P. Special Branch. The undersigned communicated
with D.S.I. Laurier, Special Branch, and learned that the
letter which was signed "Righteousness Corps" warned
the Editor of the said newspaper against publishing any
further articles against the Japanese with a warning that
should he not comply he would be decapitated in a manner
similar to Tsai Tou Tu(蔡鈞徒) whose head was found in
the French Concession on 7-2-38.

This letter was collected by the Special Branch for
comparison with two letters of a similar nature which
were received by the Editor of the Shanghai Evening Post
and Mercury and the Ta Mei Wan Pao(大美晚報) at about
8.10 p.m. 9-2-38. The letters, on examination, proved to
be all in the same handwriting.

A copy of the letter with further details is to
be forwarded to this station by the Special Branch
tomorrow (11-2-38).

When further questioned Mr. Cumine and staff stated
that they knew of no political motive which might be
attached to the case and that no article which should
warrant such an incident had been published in their
paper for or against the Japanese or Chinese.

The office was inaugurated on 27-1-1938 and today
the 15th issue of the paper was delivered.
pages.zh:
1/第 5 页。

工部局警务处特务处。本人与特务处督察 Laurier 联系，获悉该信署名为“正义团”，警告该报编辑不得再发表任何反日文章，并警告若不遵从，他将像蔡钧徒（Tsai Tou Tu）一样被斩首，蔡的头颅于 1938 年 2 月 7 日在法租界被发现。

特务处已收取该信，以便与《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）及《大美晚报》（Ta Mei Wan Pao）编辑于 1938 年 2 月 9 日晚上约 8:10 收到的两封性质类似的信件进行比对。经检查，这些信件均出自同一人手笔。

特务处将于明日（1938 年 2 月 11 日）将该信的副本及更多详情转送本捕房。

经进一步询问，Cumine 先生及职员表示，他们不知道本案可能涉及任何政治动机，他们的报纸近期也未发表过任何足以引发此类事件的亲日或反日、亲华或反华文章。

该办公室于 1938 年 1 月 27 日开业，今日发行了第 15 期报纸。

pages.en:
1/Sheet No. 6.

Fragments of the missile found at the scene were
brought to the station.

The nearest policeman to the scene was C.P.C.3219
on duty at the corner of Foochow and Fokien Roads, about
30 yards distant. This C.P.C. was attracted to the
scene by the sound of the explosion and, on learning of
what had happened, he conducted a search for the culprit
in the vicinity but no trace of him could be found.

The D.O."A" and D.D.O."A" attended the scene and
also Mr. Fairbairn, i/c of a riot squad.

(An incident of a similar nature occurred at

Tang Tse Ching
Shanghai // C.D.S. 47.
Louza Station 10-2-38 Clerk Hu Pang Yau

My name is Tang Tse Ching, age 22, native of Shanghai,
residing at No. 154 Mohawk Road, employed as an apprentice at the
Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper, No.436 Foochow Road.
At about 6.00p.m. on the 10-2-38, whilst I was standing
facing Foochow Road in the downstairs office of the above mention-
ed newspaper, I suddenly saw a male wearing blue cotton cloth
short jacket and pants, dark square unshaved face, height about
5' 7/8", long hair uncombed, appeared to be of the coolie class,
enter the door and, raising his right hand he threw a hand
grenade onto the counter. The grenade first struck a desk
inside the counter, then hit my body, and fell on the cement
floor where it exploded about five seconds later. During the
interval I managed to escape from being injured by the explosion.
Inside the office at the time of the explosion were
Zung Deng Hsien, Siau Yue Ching, Pih Ts Feng, Wu Chin Chih, Ling
Tsao Wei and Ayung Yong Tse. The former three named were
wounded by the explosion while the latter three named, owing to
them being a little far away from the place of explosion, were
not injured.
The above is a true statement.

(Sgd) Tang Tse Ching.

唐子清
上海 // 刑事侦缉处 47。
老闸捕房 1938 年 2 月 10 日 书记员胡邦耀

我叫唐子清，22 岁，上海人，居住在莫霍克路 154 号，受雇于福州路 436 号《标准中文日报》（Standard Chinese Language Daily Newspaper）担任学徒。1938 年 2 月 10 日下午 6:00 左右，当我站在上述报馆楼下办公室面向福州路时，我突然看见一名男子走进门来，他身穿蓝色棉布短夹克和裤子，面色黝黑方正，未刮胡须，身高约 5 英尺 7/8 英寸，长发凌乱，看起来像是苦力阶层。他举起右手，将一枚手榴弹扔向柜台。手榴弹先击中柜台内的一张书桌，然后撞到我的身体，落在水泥地板上，约五秒后爆炸。在此期间，我设法躲避，未在爆炸中受伤。
爆炸发生时，办公室内有宗登贤（音译）、萧月清（音译）、毕茨峰（音译）、吴金芝（音译）、凌造伟（音译）和阿勇永子（音译）。前三人被爆炸炸伤，而后三人因距离爆炸地点稍远，未受伤。
以上陈述属实。

（签名）唐子清。

Det. Sgt. P.M. Yankovsky, French Police attended the

Subject Hand grenade exploded in front of the Chung Hwa Literary and Art
Society (中華学藝社), French Concession.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I

At 11.15 p.m. February 9, a missile was thrown
by some unknown person and exploded on the sidewalk in
front of house No. 45 Rue Victor Emmanuel III. No person
was injured and the motive for the outrage is unknown.

House No. 45 Rue Victor Emmanuel III, generally
known as the offices of the Chung Hwa Literary and Art
Society, at present is occupied by the Chiao Tung Univer-
sity, the premises of the university, located on Avenue
Haig, in the meantime being used as a refugee camp.

The Chiao Tung University moved into this house
in the beginning of January, 1938, when the Chung Hwa
Literary and Art Society suspended its activities following
the withdrawal of Chinese troops from the Shanghai area.

The Chung Hwa Literary and Art Society first came
into existence in 1916, sponsored by Chinese students living
in Japan, and was named the "Ping Zung Zoe" (丙辰学社). In
1920, a head office was opened in Shanghai, and a few years
later, the present title was adopted. The object of this
Society is for mutual improvement in scientific knowledge.
The membership was small to start with, but has gradually
increased, and at present, it has some 850 members, including
a number of Chinese officials. Among the committee members
and directors of the Society are the following :-

Chen Li-fu (陈立夫), member of the Standing
Committee of the C.E.C. of the Kuomintang.

Pan Kung-chun (潘公展), Chief of the Bureau of
Social Affairs, Shanghai.

2 月 9 日晚上 11:15，一枚投掷物被某不明身份者抛出，并在维克多·艾曼纽尔三世路 45 号门前的人行道上爆炸。无人受伤，作案动机不明。

维克多·艾曼纽尔三世路 45 号，通常被称为中华学艺社办公室，目前由交通大学占用，该大学位于海格路的校舍 meanwhile 正被用作难民收容所。

交通大学于 1938 年 1 月初搬入此屋，当时随着中国军队撤出上海地区，中华学艺社停止了活动。

中华学艺社最初成立于 1916 年，由旅居日本的中国学生发起，名为“丙辰学社”（Ping Zung Zoe）。1920 年，在上海设立了总部，几年后采用了现在的名称。该社的宗旨是促进科学知识的相互提高。会员起初很少，但逐渐增加，目前约有 850 名会员，其中包括一些中国官员。该社的委员和董事包括以下人员：

陈立夫，国民党中常会委员。

潘公展，上海市社会局局长。

| | Hand Grenade thrown at the Moore Memorial Church. | |

At 7.00p.m. 2-2-38 a telephone message was received from the Moore Memorial Church, to the effect that a bomb had exploded at the Church.

Enquiries by C.D.S. 274 and D.T. Macadie ascertained that at 6.55 p.m. a hand grenade exploded at the east end of the cloisters along the south side of the Church facing Hankow Road. Portions of the grenade picked up at the scene showed it to be of the "potato-masher" type. The missile struck the wall of the Church Wall about six inches from the ground under a stone seat which apparently deadened the explosion with a result that apart from slight damage to the masonry, only two panes of glass of a fanlight of the door at the end of the cloisters were damaged. No person was nearby at the time and no one was injured. A number of cars are parked on Hankow Road outside the side of the Church and a person standing between these cars could have hurled the grenade over the wall of the Church compound. The distance between the Hankow Road wall and the spot in question is about 20 feet. C.P.C. 2489 was on duty on the traffic lights at the corner of Hankow and Yu Ya Ching Roads and immediately on hearing the explosion switched off his lights and ran eastwards down Hankow

1938 年 2 月 2 日晚上 7:00，接到慕尔纪念堂的电话留言，称教堂发生炸弹爆炸。

经刑事侦缉处警员 274 号和侦探 T. Macadie 查询，查明下午 6:55，一枚手榴弹在教堂南侧面向汉口路的回廊东端爆炸。在现场捡到的手榴弹碎片显示其为“土豆捣碎器”式（即柄式手榴弹）。投掷物击中离地面约六英寸的教堂墙壁，位于一个石凳下方，该石凳显然减弱了爆炸威力，结果是除了砖石轻微受损外，仅回廊尽头门上的两扇气窗玻璃受损。当时附近无人，无人受伤。许多汽车停在教堂侧面外的汉口路上，站在这些汽车之间的人本可以将手榴弹扔过教堂院墙。汉口路围墙与该地点之间的距离约为 20 英尺。华捕 2489 号当时正在汉口路与虞洽卿路路口的交通信号灯处执勤，听到爆炸声后立即关闭信号灯，沿汉口路向东跑去

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of C.P.C. 2489 Tsang Foh Sung (曾佛松), age 30,
native of Shantung taken by me
translated
at Louza Stn. on the 2-2-38 and interpreted by Clerk Tang.

I beg to report the following:
At 6.55.p.m. 2-2-38, I was detailed on Traffic Lights duty
at the Corner of Yu Ya Ching and Hankow Roads. Immediately on
hearing the explosion in the vicinity of the side gate of the Moore
Memorial Church on Hankow Road, I ran down to the scene but no
trace could be found from elsewhere. Following which, I then ran
inside the front door of the Church, where I asked one Chinese
standerby as to whether had any riot been occurred inside the
Church, to which, he replied 'no'.
Not soon after I resumed my duty, Chinese and Foreign
detectives were arriving to the scene for making enquiries.
Later I knew that a bomb had exploded inside the side gate
of the Church, on Hankow Road.
The above is my true statement.

Signed and cross marked: Tsang Foh Sung.

警方调查报告。

以下为华籍巡长 2489 号曾佛松（Tsang Foh Sung），30岁，山东籍，于1938年2月2日在老闸捕房由本人录取、经职员 Tang 翻译的陈述。

谨报告如下：
1938年2月2日下午6时55分，我被派往江西路与汉口路拐角处执行交通信号灯执勤任务。一听到汉口路摩尔纪念教堂（Moore Memorial Church）侧门附近传来爆炸声，我立即跑向现场，但从其他地方未发现任何踪迹。随后，我跑进教堂前门，询问一名在场的中国人教堂内是否发生了骚乱，他回答“没有”。
不久后我恢复执勤，中外侦探陆续抵达现场进行调查。后来我得知，一枚炸弹在汉口路教堂的侧门内爆炸。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名并画押：曾佛松。

The scene of this offence is the Dzing Kwong(光
小 ) Primary School, No.12 and 12A Tongkushau
Gardens.

The Principal is Dr. Shih Un Joh(謝恩祿),
Cantonese, who is at present in Canton. The conpt.
is temporarily in charge of the buildings, where
110 young students attend daily.

There are four other teachers employed on the
premises, as follows:
Chung Ts Pan(陳樹楠), male, Cantonese.
Wok Ying Sung(郭萍生), female, Cantonese.
Lieu Lyung Lien(刘筠碧 ), female, Cantonese.
Shah To Ngoh(謝志嬌), female, Cantonese.
All reside in the school.

At 8-30pm. on 5/7/58 one Oh Ho Cho(歐奉漳),
Formosan, Dentist practising at No.72 Nanking Road,
attended this station and reported that at about 10pm
on 2/7/58 he was in his room on the ground floor of
House No.12A when there was a large explosion at the
front door. He ran to the door and found that the
glass panels had been shattered and a hole in the
cement at the entrance. He intended to report to the
police at that time, but the complainant and other
teachers prevailed on him to keep the matter secret
for the sake of the students.

As being afraid of further incidents, he attended
this station today.

J.P.C. Sugimoto, Powell Station, aided in
enquiries.

Bomb Explosion in front of the "Sin Wan Pao".

With reference to the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch)
on the attached crime diary, enquiries made by the undersigned
show that the rumours to the effect that the management of the
"Sin Wan Pao" (新闻报) had received a sum of $50,000 as a
consideration to refrain from publishing anti-Japanese
literature in its paper are absolutely groundless.

The capital of the paper is $2,000,000; it make huge
profits every year. Consequently, every employee, from the
general manager and chief editor down to the office coolie,
is given an annual bonus equivalent to about five months' pay
and vacancies caused by the deaths of employees are often filled
by the children of the deceased. From the time it was estab-
lished up to the present time, the paper has never dabbled in
politics, nor has it ever received any subsidies. This
policy won for it much public confidence. The present
General Manager is Mr. Wang Pah-ji (汪伯奇) who took over
the post upon the death of his father, Mr. Wang Han-chi
(汪漢溪). He is assisted by Mr. Wang Chung-wei (汪仲韋),
the Assistant Manager, who is the younger son of the late Wang
Han-chi. The Wang brothers are also shareholders of the
paper; their integrity is unquestioned. They have never done
anything to give offence to others nor are they interested in
politics.

After the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from
Shanghai and vicinity, the "Sin Wan Pao" suspended the
publication of leading articles or comments and proofs of all
reading matter were sent to the Shanghai Newspaper Censorship
Bureau in Hardoon Building, Nanking Road, for censorship.

Crime. The undersigned questioned Mr. Tong Lung Mei regarding the motive for this attack on the newspaper but he could not explain the same as he does not see any reason for such action.

He stated that in December 1935, the newspaper was not published for 4 days owing to the trouble among employees of the same, but as soon as the trouble was settled on December 21st the newspaper was again printed as usual. The management of the newspaper never received any threatening letter or warning of political nature.

It appears from the enquiries that the management of the Sin Wen Pao usually forward the proofs of their newspaper to the office of the Japanese Censorship Bureau, Maroon Building, for their approval.

Several fragments of the hand-grenade and wooden handle of the same had been picked up by the undersigned outside the building of the newspaper and the same will be forwarded to the Finger Print Bureau for examination.

The World's Chinese Students' Federation came into existence as early as 1905, through the efforts of Dr. T.H. Lee, founder of the Fu Tan University, Dr. W.W. Yen, until recently Chinese Ambassador to U.S.S.R., and other notable Chinese educationalists. Its present offices are situated at No.191 Carter Road.

The object of the Federation is to promote friendship among students who wish to study abroad and who are members, also mutual assistance and furthering of studies of its members. The Federation gives advice and renders all necessary service to Chinese students proceeding abroad to study, assists unemployed students in finding employment, publishes periodicals and also gives lectures.

During the past thirty years the Federation has proved itself to be very valuable to Chinese students going abroad, giving the necessary assistance in obtaining passports, booking passage tickets and making general enquiries for them. Students who have availed themselves of its services have found their influence very useful.

Prior to the local hostilities, a weekly lecture was held on the premises every Saturday and enjoyed a wide range of popularity being favourably commented on by students attending.

Beside undertaking the above work, the Federation also accommodates several educational institutions among them are (1) The Wei Jiu (World) Primary School, (2). The Wei Jiu English Evening School, and (3). The Wei Jiu English and Chinese Typewriting School, with a total attendance

该联合会的宗旨是促进有志出国留学的学生会员之间的友谊，以及会员间的互助和学业进修。联合会为出国留学的中国学生提供建议并办理一切必要服务，协助失业学生寻找工作，出版刊物，并举办讲座。

在过去三十年中，事实证明该联合会对出国留学的中国学生极具价值，为他们获取护照、预订船票以及进行一般查询提供了必要的协助。曾利用其服务的学生发现其影响力非常有益。

在本地战事爆发前，每周六在该处所举行一次讲座，广受欢迎，出席的学生给予了好评。

除开展上述工作外，该联合会还容纳了几家教育机构，其中包括 (1) 维久小学，(2) 维久英语夜校，以及 (3) 维久中英文打字学校，总入学人数

Mr. Tsu Sau Ping (朱少屏), Principal of the Wei
Jeu Primary School, 101 Carter Road, was interviewed
this a.m. 2-2-38, by the undersigned, and questioned,
with a view to discovering the motive for the bomb-
throwing.

As a result of this interview the undersigned
learned that Mr. Tsu was educated in Japan, and, has
numerous Japanese friends in Shanghai, but does not
take an active part in any committee meetings, neither
has he been invited to participate in any organisation/s
associated in any way with the Japanese.

The general demeanour, appearance, manner of speech
and dress would quite easily deceive any person into
deeming Mr. Tsu a Japanese subject. Possibly his long
associations with the Japanese being responsible for his
unconscious mannerisms has lead some person/s to believe
him either a Japanese subject, or, it has become known
that he has certain Japanese connections, hence the
warning bomb thrown into the doorway. That this was
intended more as a warning than otherwise is deduced
from the fact that the person throwing the potato-masher
had only to walk through the front door about 12 feet
and he would then be able to throw the bomb into Mr.
Tsu's own study or office.

This school is used by the Worlds Chinese Students
Federation, and Mr. Tsu is actually the Principal, also

通过此次问话，下署人获悉朱先生曾在日本受教育，在上海有许多日本朋友，但他并不积极参加任何委员会会议，也未受邀参与任何与日本人有任何关联的组织。

其总体举止、外貌、言谈方式和着装很容易让人误以为朱先生是日本臣民。或许是他长期与日本人交往导致的无意识习惯动作，使某些人认为他是日本臣民，或者是因为已知他与日本人有某种联系，因此才向门口投掷警告性炸弹。推断此举更多是作为一种警告而非其他目的，依据是投掷者只需穿过前门行走约12英尺，便能将炸弹扔进朱先生的书房或办公室。

Police immediately searched the vicinity resulting
in the finding of a wooden handle and a string with a
brass ring attached, obviously parts of the hand grenade.
The wooden handle was picked up in the doorway whilst the
string was found about 70 yards South of the scene,
(on the footpath) suggesting that the culprit escaped
in that direction.

Exhaustive enquiries were made by detectives in nearby
shops, amongst various ricksha coolies, pedestrians,
etc. but nothing useful could be learnt.

A party of detectives was immediately dispatched to
search all lodging houses and hotels in Sinza District,
but without result.

One named Tsu Hoong Ching (朱洪卿), 25, son of the
principal of the above named school was interviewed and
he stated that he was unable to locate his father, who
had left the school at about 2p.m. today and had not yet
returned home. Tsu Hoong Ching states that as far as
he knows his father has no Japanese connections whatever
and is not concerned with any political organizations,
but he would locate his father as soon as possible when
the undersigned would then be able to interview him.

No damage. No arrests. Motive at present unknown.
D.D.O. "B" informed. Special Branch informed.

侦探在附近的商店、各类人力车夫、行人等中间进行了详尽的询问，但未获得任何有用信息。

一队侦探立即被派往搜索新闸区的所有旅馆和酒店，但毫无结果。

一名名为朱洪卿（Tsu Hoong Ching），25岁，系上述学校校长之子的男子接受了问话，他表示无法找到其父亲，其父于今日下午2点左右离开学校，尚未回家。朱洪卿表示，据他所知，其父与日本人没有任何联系，也不参与任何政治组织，但他会尽快找到其父亲，以便下署人随后对其进行问话。

At 7.10p.m. 27-1-38, a telephone message was
received from C.P.C. 3305 reporting that a hand
grenade had been thrown in the Hung Lee Candy Shop,
No. 299 Burkill Road.

On receipt of the above report C.D.C. 54 and the
undersigned immediately proceeded to the scene of the
crime and ascertained same to be a three storied
Chinese dwelling house situated on the South side
of Burkill Road about 50 yards from Park Road.

The ground floor of the premises are occupied by
the complainant and his assistant namely Ling Ong
Sung, age 47 years, native of Canton and Chue Ji 'oh,
age 32 years, native of Canton, who utilize the front
of the premises for selling home made sweets.

The second floor of the premises are occupied by
3 families.

(1) Ling Sz (林氏), age 49 years, native of Canton,
widow, and her daughter named Yau Ying (尤英),
age 24 years, native of Canton, S/Cabaret dancer.

(2) Yue Yue Sing (袁友兴), age 32 years, native of
Ningpo, S/Clerk employed in the Anderson Myers
Co.

(3) Sung Yan Yung (沈仁根), age 33 years, native of
Ningpo, S/shop-assistant employed in the Zeu
Dzong Dong Chinese Medicine Shop.

3rd Floor:
Occupied by one named Tsoong Sz Ing (鐘志英), age
68 years, native of Canton, and his wife, the
former being employed by the Wing On Co., Nanking
Road as a ticket collector in the Chinese Amuse-
ment Centre.

1938年1月27日晚上7点10分，接到巡捕 C.P.C. 3305 的电话报告，称有一枚手榴弹被投掷进伯基尔路（Burkill Road）299号的恒利糖果店。

收到上述报告后，刑侦警员 C.D.C. 54 及下文签署人立即前往犯罪现场，经确认，现场为一栋位于伯基尔路南侧、距公园路（Park Road）约50码的三层中式住宅。

该处所的一楼由报案人及其助手占用，即林兴森（Ling Ong Sung），47岁，广东人；以及许其芳（Chue Ji 'oh，音译），32岁，广东人，他们利用处所的前部售卖自制糖果。

该处所的二楼由三个家庭占用。

(1) 林氏（Ling Sz），49岁，广东人，寡妇，及其女儿尤英（Yau Ying），24岁，广东人，职业为舞女。

(2) 袁友兴（Yue Yue Sing），32岁，宁波人，职业为安德森·迈尔斯公司（Anderson Myers Co.）职员。

(3) 沈仁根（Sung Yan Yung），33岁，宁波人，职业为聚宗东中药店（Zeu Dzong Dong Chinese Medicine Shop，音译）店员。

三楼：
由钟志英（Tsoong Sz Ing），68岁，广东人，及其妻子占用，前者受雇于南京路永安公司，在华人大世界（Chinese Amusement Centre）担任检票员。

The actual details regarding the offence are as
follows:-
At about 7.5p.m. 27-1-38, whilst Ling Ong Sung
(林旺森) & Shue Ji Foh (许其芳) were standing in the
showroom of the Hung Lee sweet shop examining account
books they heard a loud explosion, then observed clouds
of smoke, neither concerned were injured but admitted
that they suffered from shock and did not attempt to
move. After the lapse of about two minutes C.P.C. 3305
ran into the shop, he having been attracted therein by
the explosion, at which time he was standing on Burkill
Road and Park Road corner (patrolling 9 and 11 Beat,
1 Section).
On the arrival of the police officer the complainant
and his assistant partly recovered from the shock with
the result that they explained the occurrence to C.P.C.
3305 and he telephoned to Sinza Police Station as
outlined above.
The investigating detectives carefully questioned
pedestrians and persons living in the vicinity of the
offence, but no information or witnesses could be
obtained and the complainant and his apprentice state
that they did not observe the person who threw the
hand grenade.
No persons were injured, and the hand grenade appears
to have been thrown onto 6 tins of syrup (each weighing

关于该罪行的具体细节如下：-
1938年1月27日晚上7点05分左右，当林旺森（Ling Ong Sung，音译，注：前文为林兴森）和许其芳（Shue Ji Foh，音译，注：前文为Chue Ji 'oh）站在恒利糖果店的展厅内查阅账簿时，他们听到一声巨大的爆炸声，随后看到浓烟，两人均未受伤，但承认受到惊吓，未敢移动。大约两分钟后，巡捕 C.P.C. 3305 跑进店内，他是被爆炸声吸引而来的，当时他正站在伯基尔路和公园路的拐角处（在第1区第9和第11巡段巡逻）。
警官到达后，报案人及其助手从惊吓中部分恢复，随即向 C.P.C. 3305 说明了情况，后者按上述内容致电静安寺捕房。
调查侦探仔细询问了行人及居住在案发地附近的人员，但未获得任何信息或证人，报案人及其学徒表示他们没有观察到投掷手榴弹的人。
无人受伤，手榴弹似乎是扔在了6听糖浆上（每听重

The damage to the premises and contents was trivial,

6 pieces of shrapnel was found in the showroom whilst

pectable working individuals and not concerned with

The complainant is a refugee from Hongkew and was

50斤），这些糖浆于1938年1月27日上午9点30分存放在该处所的展厅内。

处所及内部物品的损坏微不足道，弹片穿透了2听糖浆和一个木制隔板。

在展厅内发现了6块弹片，同时在伯基尔路上，距离犯罪现场正门约5码处，发现了一段长约10英寸的细绳，一端系着一个明显是新制的铜环，另一端系着一条长约1英寸、宽½英寸的薄钢条，形状像一把钳子，下半部分经过打火石处理以便点火。

经讯问，屋内所有人似乎都是正派的务工人员，与政治毫无关联，同时报案人声称他于1938年1月25日开设恒利糖果店，此后未收到任何威胁等。

报案人是虹口的难民，此前曾在浦东的王忠林木行（Vong Chong Lumbe Yard，音译，一家现已毁于火灾的中资公司）担任木匠。

关于糖浆罐的问询中，报案人声称他于1938年1月27日上午9点30分从一名身份不明的中国经纪人处购买，他以

At the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities
and prior to opening his present business the complain-
ant operated a small sweet shop on Avenue Road near

Enquiries appear to suggest that the thrower of the

BOMB THROWN ON BREMAN PIECE.

At 11.05 a.m. 10/1/38 a telephone message was received from C.P.C. 865 on duty at Brenan Piece telephone box to the effect that a bomb had been thrown.

S.I.Darville and D.S.Deaville, D.S.I. Tang immediately attended.

Insptr. West and D.I. Toon attended a few minutes later when it was ascertained that at about 11 a.m. 10/1/38 a bomb (cigarette tin type) had been thrown by some unknown person and had dropped about two yards from where the Italian soldier on duty was standing, fortunately no one was injured.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 11 JAN. 1938）

A thorough search of the surrounding premises was immediately made by members of the Japanese Military Police, but without result.

From fragments of the missile which were picked up in the vicinity, it appears that same was similar to those thrown elsewhere, i.e. bomb made by use of "Ruby Queen" cigarette tin, containing small porcelain jar and fragments of metal and glass.

General enquiries in the vicinity failed to ascertain by whom the bomb had been thrown or from what direction, but a general survey of the scene seems to indicate that the most likely place would have been from one of the rooms of the second floor of ...

1.

炸弹投掷在布伦南弄（Brenan Piece）。

1938年1月10日上午11点05分，接到在布伦南弄电话亭执勤的巡捕 C.P.C. 865 的电话消息，称有人投掷了炸弹。

西德维尔（Darville）高级督察、迪维尔（Deaville）侦探警长及唐（Tang）副督察长立即到场。

韦斯特（West）督察及图恩（Toon）侦探督察几分钟后到场，经查实，1938年1月10日上午11点左右，一名身份不明者投掷了一枚炸弹（香烟罐类型），落在正在执勤的意大利士兵站立处约两码远的地方，幸运的是无人受伤。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别课 1938年1月11日）

日本宪兵队成员立即对周围处所进行了彻底搜查，但一无所获。

从附近捡到的导弹碎片来看，它与其他地方投掷的炸弹相似，即使用“红女王”（Ruby Queen）香烟罐制成的炸弹，内含小瓷罐及金属和玻璃碎片。

在附近进行的普遍调查未能查明炸弹由谁投掷或来自哪个方向，但对现场的总体勘察似乎表明，最可能的地点是来自……二楼的其中一个房间

（批注及印章区域文字模糊，难以辨认，此处转录不清）

Sse Yang Teashop, 979 (Chinese No.) Jessfield Road,
which is only about 10 yards from the scene.
The proprietor Tse Ru Tsong ( 徐復忠 ) and his
assistants were carefully questioned but could not
assist the police in any way.
C.P.C. 865 and C.P.C. 2711 on post duty on Brenan
Place were at the scene at the time of the incident
but on questioning both stated that they were unaware
of same until they heard the explosion.
The cordon which was thrown round the vicinity by
the Japanese Military Police was withdrawn at 12.05
p.m. when traffic resumed its normal course, no
untoward incident occurred.
It is worthy of note that from enquiries made it
was ascertained that there were no Japanese in the
vicinity at the time of the incident.
D.O."B" and D.D.O."B" informed and attended.
Fragments of the bomb will be forwarded to C.4.

四杨茶馆（Sse Yang Teashop，音译），兆丰路（Jessfield Road）979号（中国门牌），距离现场仅约10码。
店主徐復忠（Tse Ru Tsong）及其助手接受了仔细讯问，但未能以任何方式协助警方。
事发时在布伦南弄（Brenan Place）岗位执勤的巡捕 C.P.C. 865 和 C.P.C. 2711 均在现场，但经讯问，两人均表示在听到爆炸声之前对此事毫不知情。
日本宪兵队在周围设立的警戒线于中午12点05分撤除，交通恢复正常，未发生其他意外事件。
值得注意的是，经查询证实，事发时附近没有日本人。

兆丰路1165弄内的一个容器中，看到一个顶部用胶带缠绕的香烟罐，他用一根竹竿击打该罐，导致其爆炸，造成其手部和面部受伤。
被送往红十字会医院，医生诊断书称：“面部和手部有弹片伤，不是很严重”，包扎后该男子获准离开。
经查看现场，发现其沿兆丰路距离布伦南弄（Brenen Piece，原文拼写）约300码，垃圾容器位于弄堂内约20码处。

pages.en:
Chinese Leaders Living
Under Threat Of Murder
By Terrorists' Gunmen

Activities Of Powerful Secret Society Indicated
In Series Of Assassinations And Bomb Attacks
Last Month In Settlement And Concession

BULLETS SENT IN LETTERS TO MANY
PROMINENT BUSINESS MEN HERE

Marked by a powerful and well-organized secret society of terrorists and gunmen, numerous Shanghai Chinese business leaders are living under the threat of death, warned of their peril by a single bullet sent anonymously to them by mail. Sometimes the bullet is accompanied by a note of accusation, but often there is no other indication of their danger than the lead pellet.

Light on what is believed to be but a minor part of this terrorist organization was thrown early yesterday morning by the French Police, when they succeeded in rounding up four Chinese, one of whom was carrying the dreaded warning in an unaddressed letter, and who made a confession which led to the arrest of the other three.

Two guns were seized by the French Police in the course of their raids, but of more importance is the fact that for the first time some tangible proof has been obtained of the existence of the organization, and both Concession and Settlement authorities are eagerly pursuing the slender clues furnished by the suspects.

It has for long been recognized by the authorities that an organized terrorist society has been in existence in Shanghai, but so carefully have its secrets been guarded that the closest interrogation of various suspects have failed to supply leading clues and despite the most relentless hunt ever staged by the Police in the history of Shanghai they were unable to make progress towards locating the headquarters of the organization.

Attacks Linked

Hints of the extent of the organization's influence and power have been indicated from time to time by series of assassinations and bombing attacks in the Settlement and Concession, and by the similarity of methods which have linked almost every case together, particularly in the bombing outrages.

Practically all of the bombs which have been thrown since the first major outbreak on New Year's day have been of the same type and of similar construction, a fact which makes it obviously that if the bombs were not made by one "factory" then they were made according to a common plan.

The most remarkable feature of the missiles, apart from various peculiarities of their construction, is that they are so weak as to be incapable of inflicting fatal wounds unless the explosion took place at very close quarters to the victim. Enclosed in cigarette tins generally bearing the "Ruby Queen" label, the explosive material is of poor quality and small quantity, while the "shrapnel" may be composed of anything from broken glass to jagged pieces of metal of all descriptions.

Although the reports still lack confirmation, it was at one time stated that even Japanese officials had received threatening letters, and it is known for certain that literally scores of Chinese have received them.

Concession Arrests

Of the four men arrested by the French Police, one was found to be in possession of one of these letters, still unaddressed. The man was taken as a suspected person on Rue Montauban at 8 p.m. on Friday, and, following the discovery of the letter, was closely questioned. A confession sent the police to Route Frelupt, where they arrested Ko Tien-fu, believed to be the leader of a "cell" in the organization.

It was on the instructions of Ko, according to the first suspect, that he was to mail the envelope to a prominent Chinese in the Concession. It was also divulged that Ko had distributed similar envelopes to all of his men, at least two others of whom were caught in the French Police net during the night.

Ko was stated by the French Police yesterday to have confessed that he was the leader of his group, but declared that there was still another man above him, but although the authorities immediately raided the address given, the "higher man" had flown.

Little Damage Done

The theory is held, on account of the weakness of the bombs, that they are intended as a threat rather than to kill, and this theory is further borne out by the fact that many of the missiles thrown recently have fallen outside houses and in the street, rather than at any point where they could do much material damage. None of the numerous bombs collected by the Police authorities in various raids has proved to be powerful enough to be deadly at any distance, and when thrown into the street they would have but little effect.

Of a different category, however, is the gun-carrying member of the organization, who too often has shown himself to be a deadly shot and capable of carrying out his mission with startling audacity. Such a one laid low one of Shanghai's greatest philanthropists and religious leaders, Mr. Loh Pa-hong, for whom the city is still grieving.

The assassinations and two attempted assassinations have all revealed the same grim purpose behind the attacks, delivered at Chinese leaders who are suspected to have connected themselves with the rehabilitation schemes for the war-torn districts around Shanghai.

Strong Organization

The very fact that, despite the campaign carried out, the International, French and Japanese authorities individually and in co-operation have failed to uncover a solution to these brutal killings alone indicates the strength of the organization behind them. A shot is fired, a man falls, and the killer is lost in the night.

The dispatch of threatening letters to Chinese, accusing them of traitorism, is a comparatively recent development and had not been linked up with the terrorist organization until the arrests yesterday by the French police. At first it was believed that a blackmailing campaign was about to be carried out, but when demands for money failed to follow the initial letter, containing a single bullet, it became clear that there was a real threat behind it.

Suppressed Societies

Various theories have been advanced to account for the formation of the organization, but it is most probable that the group was first formed immediately after the surrounding of Shanghai by Japanese forces, and the subsequent suppression of various patriotic bodies, particularly the National Salvation Association, a group which was intensely anti-Japanese in its activities.

Forced underground by official suppression, it is believed that this group has absorbed smaller organizations in a campaign of subversive and terrorist activities against Chinese leaders who have attempted to engage with the Japanese authorities in the task of rehabilitating the areas around Shanghai.

Numerous attacks have been made since the night Mr. Loh Pa-hong was shot down outside his residence in the Concession, their chronological order being as follows.

December 30.—Mr. Loh Pa-hong, business leader, prominent Catholic and well-known philanthropist, shot down outside residence in Avenue Dubail.

January 1.—Japanese soldiers bombed at corner of Hankow and Fokien Roads.

Bomb thrown at premises of Kung Dah Cotton Mill, Singapore Road.

Bomb thrown at premises of N.W.K. Cotton Mill, Gordon Road

Bomb thrown at premises of Japan-China Spinning and Weaving Company, Pootoo Road.

January 2.—Missile thrown into garden of Japanese Consul-General's residence in Seymour Road.

Unexploded missile thrown into garden of residence of Mr. Kou Hsiang-yih, Avenue du Roi Albert.

January 14.—Mr. Y. T. Van, prominent lawyer, wounded by gunmen outside residence in Weihaivet Road.

Mr. Dau Yen-ling, director of a refugee camp, shot in Sinza Road.

January 16.—Offices of American owned newspaper "Hwa Mei Wun Pao," bombed.

（手写批注：C.J.D Ch 8/31 81 / 30/1）
pages.zh:
中国领袖生活在
恐怖分子枪手的
谋杀威胁之下

上月租界与法租界发生的一系列暗杀和炸弹袭击事件
显示出一个势力强大的秘密社团的活动迹象

寄给本地许多知名商人的信件中装有子弹

上海众多华人商界领袖正生活在死亡威胁之下，这一局面由一个势力强大且组织严密的恐怖分子和枪手秘密社团所造成，他们通过匿名邮寄单颗子弹的方式向这些人发出危险警告。有时子弹会附有一张指控便条，但往往除了这颗铅弹外，没有任何其他危险迹象。

昨天清晨，法国警察成功抓获四名华人，其中一人携带了一封未写地址的信件，信中装有这种令人恐惧的警告物，此人的供词导致另外三人被捕，从而揭开了这个恐怖组织冰山一角的真相。

法国警察在突袭行动中缴获了两支枪，但更为重要的是，首次获得了该组织存在的实质性证据，法租界和公共租界当局正急切地追查嫌疑人提供的微弱线索。

当局早已认识到上海存在一个有组织的恐怖社团，但其秘密 guarded 得如此严密，以至于对各类嫌疑人的最严厉审讯均未能提供主要线索，尽管警方开展了上海历史上最为无情的搜捕行动，仍无法在定位该组织总部方面取得进展。

袭击案件相互关联

该组织影响力和权力范围的迹象，不时通过租界和法租界发生的一系列暗杀及炸弹袭击事件显现出来，尤其是炸弹暴行中几乎每起案件都显示出相似的手法，将它们联系在一起。

自元旦首次大规模爆发以来，几乎所有被投掷的炸弹都属于同一类型且构造相似，这一事实明显表明，如果这些炸弹并非出自同一家“工厂”，也是按照统一的方案制造的。

除了构造上的各种奇特之处外，这些投射物最显著的特征是威力极弱，除非在离受害者极近的距离爆炸，否则无法造成致命伤害。这些炸弹通常封装在印有“Ruby Queen”（红宝石女王）商标的香烟罐内，炸药质量低劣且数量少，而“弹片”则由从碎玻璃到各种形状不规则的金属碎片不等。

虽然报告尚待证实，但曾有说法称甚至日本官员也收到了威胁信，而已知确有数十名华人收到了此类信件。

法租界逮捕行动

在法国警察逮捕的四名男子中，有一人被发现持有一封此类信件，且尚未填写地址。该男子于周五晚 8 点在蒙托邦路 (Rue Montauban) 作为嫌疑人被捕，在发现信件后受到严密讯问。根据供词，警察前往弗雷吕普路 (Route Frelupt)，在那里逮捕了 Ko Tien-fu（音译），此人被认为是该组织一个“小组”的头目。

据第一名嫌疑人称，他是奉 Ko 之命将信封寄给法租界一位知名华人的。此外还透露，Ko 已向所有手下分发了类似的信封，其中至少另有两人在夜间落入法国警察的法网。

法国警察昨日称，Ko 已供认自己是其团伙的头目，但声称上面还有另一个人，尽管当局立即突袭了所提供的地址，但那位“上级人物”已经潜逃。

造成的破坏甚微

鉴于炸弹威力微弱，人们认为其意图在于威胁而非杀人，这一理论进一步得到以下事实的支持：最近投掷的许多投射物落在房屋外和街道上，而非任何能造成重大物质损失的地点。警方在多次突袭中收缴的大量炸弹中，没有一枚被证明在任何距离上具有致命威力，若投掷到街道上，其效果甚微。

然而，该组织中携带枪支的成员则属于另一类，他们往往表现出致命的射击能力，并能以惊人的胆量执行任务。正是这样一个人击倒了上海最伟大的慈善家和宗教领袖之一罗伯洪 (Loh Pa-hong) 先生，全城至今仍为之哀悼。

这些暗杀和两起未遂暗杀事件都揭示了袭击背后相同的冷酷目的，针对的是那些涉嫌与上海周边战乱地区重建计划有关联的中国领袖。

组织严密

尽管国际、法国和日本当局单独或合作开展了行动，却未能揭开这些残酷杀戮背后的真相，这一事实本身就表明了幕后组织的强大实力。枪声一响，一人倒下，凶手便消失在夜色中。

向华人发送指责其叛国的威胁信是比较近期出现的情况，直到昨天法国警察实施逮捕前，并未将其与恐怖组织联系起来。起初人们认为这是一场勒索运动，但当包含单颗子弹的首封信件之后并未随之出现金钱要求时，显然可以看出背后存在着真实的威胁。

被取缔的社团

关于该组织的形成提出了各种理论，但最有可能的是，该团体是在日军包围上海以及随后取缔各种爱国团体（特别是救国会，该团体的活动具有强烈的反日性质）之后立即成立的。

由于官方的镇压而被迫转入地下，据信该团体在颠覆和恐怖活动中吸收了较小的组织，针对那些试图与日本当局合作从事上海周边地区重建工作的中国领袖。

自罗伯洪先生在法租界住所外被枪击身亡的那晚以来，发生了多起袭击事件，按时间顺序排列如下。

12月30日。— 商界领袖、著名天主教徒及知名慈善家罗伯洪 (Loh Pa-hong) 先生在杜巴伊路 (Avenue Dubail) 住所外被枪击身亡。

1月1日。— 日军在汉口路与福建路转角处遭遇炸弹袭击。

炸弹被投掷至新加坡路公大棉纺厂 premises。
